info.title: Hybrid Analysis API Docs
info.description:
Falcon Sandbox has a powerful and simple API that can be used to submit files/URLs for analysis, pull report data, but also perform advanced search queries. The API is open and free to the entire IT-security community. Here, you can not only find comprehensive documentation of all endpoints and their inner workings, but also use an API key to try out all the endpoints. If you have any questions, please use our [contact form](https://go.crowdstrike.com/HybridAnalysisRequest.html).

#### API Connectors
Get the official **Python** connector: [github](https://github.com/PayloadSecurity/VxAPI).
Get the community contributed **Ruby** connector: [github](https://github.com/picatz/falconz).

#### How do I obtain an API key?
Please visit your profile page via the top right user menu, and navigate to the API key tab. Then, press the 'Create API key' button to generate a new API key.

#### What kind of authorization levels exist?
Every API key comes with an authorization level: *restricted*, *default*, *elevated* and *super*. Based on your privilege, a variety of endpoints will become accessible. By default, all free non-vetted accounts can issue restricted keys to search the database. These can then be upgraded to full default keys allowing access to data downloads (e.g. malware samples).

#### How do I authenticate on the HTTP requests?
The new API v2 only supports one way of authentication. Please send a request header as following: `api-key: [generated key]`.

#### Do you have an easy-to-use Python library/tool to interact with the API?
Yes, we have an excellent open source wrapper library [VxAPI](https://www.github.com/payloadsecurity/VxAPI) that covers all major API endpoints available here. We recommend using the '-v' flag to see the full HTTP communication on the endpoint that you are interested in. Furthermore, we also recommend checking out some of our [Knowledge Base](/knowledge-base) articles that cover interacting with the API.

#### What is the quota of my API key?
The quota of your API key will be displayed either in the 'Quota' row of the 'API key' tab or - preferably - obtain the exact details in the response header.

## Changelog

### v2.38.0
#### Deprecation Notice
- All `/file-collection/*` endpoints are now marked as deprecated. They are no longer supported after **August 21, 2026** and will return a `410 Gone` status code on or after that date.

### v2.37.0
#### Enhanced Response
- Added `detonation_parameters` field to `SampleSummary` response class

### v2.36.1
#### Enhanced Response
- Added `warnings` field to `SampleSummary` response class

### v2.36.0
#### Enhanced Quick Scan Results
- Added `vipre` Quick Scan results to the `scanners_v2` map in the `FileCollectionQuickScan`, `UrlQuickScan`, `QuickScan`, and `Overview` response classes.

### v2.35.0
#### New Endpoints
- Introduced new endpoint:
  - `GET /search/hash` which replaces the previous POST method for hash searches.

#### Deprecation Notice
- The `POST /search/hash` endpoint is now marked as deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It has been replaced by `GET /search/hash`.
- The `/report/summary` endpoint is now marked as deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

### v2.34.0
#### New Endpoints
- Introduced new endpoint:
  - `/report/{id}/dropped-files-v2` which returns all extracted/dropped binaries as a zip file.
#### Deprecation Notice
- The `/report/{id}/dropped-files` endpoint is now marked as deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It has been replaced by `/report/{id}/dropped-files-v2`. In contrary to new endpoint, the deprecated one returned **gzip-compressed** extracted/dropped binaries in a zip file.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Type of requested content, available types:
     - **xml** - The XML report as application/xml content and *.gz compressed.
     - **json** - The JSON report as application/json content
     - **html** - The HTML report as text/html content and *.gz compressed
     - **pdf** - The PDF report as application/pdf content
     - **maec** - The MAEC (4.1) report as application/xml content
     - **stix** - The STIX report as application/xml content
     - **misp** - The MISP XML report as application/xml content
     - **misp-json** - The MISP JSON report as application/json content
     - **openioc** - The OpenIOC (1.1) report as application/xml content
     - **bin** - The binary sample as application/octet-stream and *.gz compressed. Note: if the file was uploaded with 'no_share_vt' (i.e. not shared), this might fail.
     - **crt** - The binary sample certificate file (is available) as application/octet-stream content
     - **memory** - The process memory dump files as application/octet-stream and zip compressed.
     - **pcap** - The PCAP network traffic capture file as application/octet-stream and *.gz compressed.

state.description:
state field in case of archive/container:
    - If all children are IN_QUEUE, parent is IN_QUEUE
    - A child is processed, if the state is SUCCESS or ERROR
    - If at least one child is IN_PROGRESS, the parent is IN_PROGRESS
    - If all children are processed and have a mixed state, the parent is PARTIAL_SUCCESS
    - If all children are processed and have the same state, the parent shares the same state
